stories.headline: Schumer warns of Republican advantage that could change the battle for Senate control
stories.note: Chuck Schumer sent his Senate Democrats a worried letter asking "Can Republicans buy the Senate?" as the GOP's huge money edge piles up three weeks before Election Day.
body: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer sent a letter to his Democratic colleagues this week claiming his party is winning the message war, but admitting one big Republican edge has him worried: money.

Schumer framed the final weeks of the race as a collision between voter frustration with Republicans and what he called an "unprecedented tsunami of Republican money," and he warned that whichever side wins out could decide who controls the Senate.

The numbers back up his concern. According to FEC filings, Trump's MAGA Inc. has more than $400 million on hand and reportedly plans to spend in key Senate races like Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Elon Musk has given roughly $276 million to Republican-aligned PACs this cycle, including $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, the super PAC tied to Majority Leader John Thune.

Schumer blamed wealthy donors and the Supreme Court's June decision lifting federal limits on party spending for candidates. Democrats aren't broke, though: Schumer-aligned Senate Majority PAC raised a record $151 million last quarter, and the DSCC committed $40 million to battleground states, while the NRSC lined up more than $46 million of its own.
NRSC spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin called it a "pity pitch" and said it showed Republican grassroots donors are fired up "to stop Democrats' socialist march."

Why it matters: When the Senate's top Democrat is publicly fretting about being outgunned this late in the race, it's a sign Republicans hold a real advantage heading into the final stretch of the fight for the majority.

stories.headline: Rep Ilhan Omar's immigration history faces new scrutiny as federal investigators subpoena relatives
stories.note: The Omar investigation is widening: federal investigators have subpoenaed her sister and other relatives, and records show her staff got her official birth year changed after she entered Congress.
body: A day after Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home, the federal probe into her immigration history appears to be growing.

The New York Times reported that investigators have subpoenaed Omar's sister, Sahra Noor, and at least one other person in her family circle as they look at possible fraud and false statements in immigration paperwork. Fox News says it has also learned that multiple family members received subpoenas. The Justice Department confirmed agents carried out a court-authorized search warrant as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.

Separately, the New York Post reported that Omar's congressional staff asked the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library in May 2019 to change her listed birth year from 1981 to 1982. Omar has said she became a citizen through her father's naturalization in 2000, before she turned 18, and a former primary opponent has questioned whether she was still a minor at that point. The Times also reported investigators are looking at whether her late father lied on immigration forms.

On top of that, D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said her office is looking into Omar's financial disclosures, which at one point showed two businesses tied to her husband jumping from tens of thousands of dollars to between $6 million and $30 million before being amended. Trump said in a White House statement, "America wants answers, and we want them, NOW!"

Omar denies any wrongdoing and calls the probe an attempt to "weaponize federal law enforcement" against a political enemy. Fox notes that grand jury subpoenas don't by themselves mean anyone is suspected of a crime, and earlier inquiries into her history didn't lead to charges.
Why it matters: Each new development keeps one of the Democrats' most polarizing figures in the headlines just weeks before the midterms, and forces Democrats to keep answering for her.

stories.headline: 'Squad' Democrat formally introduces bill to abolish ICE, Border Patrol and dismantle DHS
stories.note: Squad member Delia Ramirez formally filed a bill to abolish ICE and Border Patrol and dismantle DHS, handing Republicans a perfect midterm contrast on border security.
body: Rep. Delia Ramirez of Illinois, a member of the progressive "Squad," has formally introduced a bill that would dismantle the Department of Homeland Security, abolish ICE and eliminate Customs and Border Protection, including Border Patrol.

Her "Reimagining Safety Act" would replace DHS with a new "Department of Community Safety." Agencies like TSA and the Coast Guard would move to the Transportation Department, FEMA and the cybersecurity agency would go to the new department, and some customs and immigration duties would be shifted to Treasury and Justice. The bill would also ban federal money for border walls starting in fiscal 2027 and order Guantánamo Bay's detention center closed within 60 days.

Cosponsors include fellow Squad member Rashida Tlaib along with Reps. Adelita Grijalva and Jim McGovern. Ramirez defended the plan, saying Americans wake up every day with "a new reason to dismantle DHS."

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin fired back that abolishing DHS is "NEVER going to happen," and the White House said "the contrast has never been clearer," pointing to Trump's record of 16 straight months of zero releases of illegal immigrants at the border.

Why it matters: With the bill now formally on the table, Republicans can point to a concrete Democratic proposal to eliminate the agencies that guard the border, a contrast the GOP is eager to draw before Election Day.

stories.headline: Trump signs pardons for Alaska diesel mechanics onstage during rally touting major energy deals
stories.note: At a fired-up Wasilla, Alaska rally, Trump pardoned diesel mechanics prosecuted under Biden and announced every federal permit is done for an 800-mile natural gas pipeline.
body: President Trump brought two Alaska diesel mechanics onstage at a midterm rally in Wasilla on Tuesday night and signed pardons for them in front of the crowd.

The men, Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming, co-own an Anchorage diesel repair shop and pleaded guilty in 2022 to conspiring to violate the Clean Air Act. The Biden Justice Department said their shop removed emissions-control equipment on at least 37 diesel vehicles. Trump said he was giving unconditional pardons to them and to Wasilla shop owner Mac Spurlock, whom he had pardoned earlier.

Trump argued their work kept trucks running in Alaska's brutal cold and called the Biden-era prosecutions unfair. Signing the papers, he took a shot at Biden's autopen and told the crowd, "What an honor. I love doing this stuff." One of the mechanics said the case had destroyed friendships and families.

The rally also featured big news on Alaska energy: Trump declared that a long-awaited 800-mile natural gas pipeline has secured every federal permit it needs, telling Alaskans they could "start tonight."
Why it matters: Trump is pairing energy wins with a message about Biden-era overreach in a state where Republicans are defending key Senate and governor races.

stories.headline: Kamala Harris faces Democratic doubts over 2028 as allies push back on claims she’s squandered her chance
stories.note: Democratic donors and strategists are openly saying Kamala Harris "totally blew it" as she weighs a 2028 run, forcing her allies onto defense.
body: As Kamala Harris weighs another run for president in 2028, a growing number of Democratic insiders are saying she has wasted her chance to reinvent herself after losing in 2024.

A Politico report based on interviews with nearly 20 California Democratic donors and strategists captured the doubts. Obama campaign veteran Doug Herman said Harris "totally blew it," and former South Carolina Gov. Jim Hodges said he sees "more of the same." An anonymous Democratic consultant told Fox that bad memories of her 2024 loss are still fresh with voters.

Harris adviser Maria Cardona fired back, calling the story silly and defending Harris' ideas. The policies she pointed to as "groundbreaking" include expanding the Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, and making D.C. and Puerto Rico states.

Fox also notes that some Democrats running in red states have asked Harris not to campaign with them this fall, even as she stumps for candidates like Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed. Another strategist, Michael Ceraso, argued consultants aren't voters and pointed out that Biden won on his third try.

Why it matters: The party's last nominee is being written off by her own side, and the agenda her defenders are touting, like packing the Court, is exactly the kind of platform Republicans want to run against.

stories.headline: Dem candidate's bizarre anti-MAGA tirade ends with 'We have guns too'
stories.note: An Indiana Democrat running for county council said she'd "fire all Republicans," called MAGA voters racist, and closed a televised forum with "We have guns too."
body: A Democrat running for county council in Fayette County, Indiana, is getting widely mocked after a rambling performance at a televised candidate forum.

Asked to name an unpopular decision she would make if elected, candidate Jaime West answered, "Fire all Republicans." She went on to call "MAGAs" racist and not very intelligent, blamed Republicans for ICE coming into communities, and claimed a sheriff's nephew had threatened to kill her.

When the moderator asked for her final message to voters, West said, "We have guns too." Conservative accounts like LibsOfTikTok questioned whether she was intoxicated, and commentator Viva Frei said the remark would ordinarily be disqualifying.

Fayette County Sheriff Zac Jones said he doesn't know West and has five nieces and zero nephews. He told Fox it's "a sad day when this is the best the Democrat Party can get" for the office. West couldn't be reached for comment.
West is running against Republican Gary Keener Jr.
Why it matters: It's a local race, but the clip is the kind of viral moment that feeds the GOP's argument that Democratic rhetoric about Trump voters has gone off the rails.

stories.headline: Major banks closed accounts of MAGA, pro-life and other conservative groups disfavored by Biden admin: bombshell report
stories.note: A new federal regulator report finds America's biggest banks debanked MAGA merchants, pro-life and religious groups, and gun businesses during the Biden years, and the CFPB is now investigating.
body: A new report from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the federal bank regulator, says the country's largest banks closed accounts and denied credit to conservative, religious and pro-Trump customers between 2020 and 2025.

The OCC's review looked at 100,000 complaints and 50,000 internal bank records. It names nine banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo, Capital One and PNC, and says they used "reputation risk" to cut off disfavored customers and industries like firearms, oil and gas, coal and private prisons.

Among the examples: JPMorgan's WePay payment service closed accounts for merchants selling MAGA and pro-Trump merchandise, and its screening system flagged terms like "MAGA" and "America First." PNC refused a credit line to a media company partly because an owner's foundation funded Christian conservative groups, and Wells Fargo declined loans to gun businesses over fears of Biden administration pressure. The report says banks often leaned on Southern Poverty Law Center "hate group" labels.

The report also found some left-leaning groups were turned away, and all nine banks told regulators they've changed their practices. JPMorgan said the WePay process "did not meet our expectations" and the business no longer operates.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau opened an investigation Wednesday. Acting Director Mark Paoletta called the tactics "thuggish," and Comptroller Jonathan Gould said the report is "irrefutable evidence" of discrimination. The review grew out of Trump's 2025 executive order against politicized debanking.

Why it matters: It's official confirmation of what conservatives have complained about for years, and it gives Republicans a strong talking point about Biden-era pressure on Americans with the wrong politics.
